title: Beauty and the Beast.
lines: In a little village in France, with little houses and a bakery and a fountain, lived a clever girl.
Her name was Belle.
And do you know what Belle loved to do most?
Read books!
Belle read all day long.
When she walked down the street, she read.
When she sat by the fountain, she read.
She read about faraway lands, about dragons and about princes.
She went to the bookshop every day.
Do you have a new book?
Yes, said the bookseller, and he gave her her favourite book as a present.
The people in the village thought Belle was a bit strange.
A girl who's always reading?
But Belle didn't mind.
A big tough man lived in the village too.
His name was Gaston.
Gaston thought he was very handsome and very strong.
He wanted to marry Belle.
But Belle thought Gaston was silly and a show-off.
No, thank you, she said.
Belle lived with her papa, Maurice.
Papa was an inventor.
He made funny machines that squeaked and whistled.
Toot!
Pfft!
One day Papa rode his horse to the market.
But he got lost in the dark forest.
Wolves howled: Awoooo!
Papa ran away, and came to a big, dark castle.
The horse came home alone.
Neigh!
Belle got a fright.
Where is Papa?
She jumped on the horse and rode to the castle.
The castle was big and cold.
The door opened.
Creeeak.
Hello?
called Belle.
And there, in a cold room, she found her papa.
But then someone came.
A big, hairy Beast with horns and teeth and a long cape.
GRRRROAAAR!
It was the Beast, the master of the castle.
Belle was scared, but also brave.
Let my papa go, she said.
Then I'll stay here.
And so Belle stayed in the castle.
But the castle was under a spell!
Long ago the Beast had been a prince.
A prince who wasn't kind.
An enchantress had turned him into a Beast.
And all the people in the castle had been turned into objects.
There was a candlestick with candles on his hands.
His name was Lumière, and he spoke with a funny French accent.
There was a clock called Cogsworth.
Tick tock!
And there was a friendly round teapot.
Her name was Mrs Potts.
She could talk, and she could pour tea.
Glug glug glug, a warm cup of tea, dear?
Her little son was a small cup with a chip.
His name was Chip, and he hopped around on the table.
Hee hee hee!
The objects made a delicious feast for Belle.
The plates danced, the forks sang, and Lumière put on a big show.
Be our guest!
Belle laughed and clapped her hands.
At first the Beast was very angry and roared a lot.
Grrr!
But Belle said: If you want me to be kind, you must be kind too.
The Beast was surprised.
Nobody had ever said that to him before.
Slowly the Beast changed.
He learned to speak gently.
He fed the little birds in the snow together with Belle.
Tweet tweet.
And one day he said: Belle, I have a surprise.
He opened a big door.
And behind it?
A huge library, full of books right up to the ceiling!
Thousands of books!
Belle couldn't believe her eyes.
This is all yours, said the Beast.
Wow!
One evening Belle put on a yellow ball gown.
The Beast wore a blue suit.
And they danced together in the big ballroom, while Mrs Potts sang softly.
But Gaston was jealous.
He came to the castle with a whole crowd of people to catch the Beast.
The objects fought back.
Lumière blew fire, and the wardrobe jumped on the people.
Hee hee hee!
They all ran away.
The Beast was hurt.
Belle cried and said: I love you.
And then something magical happened.
Ping, ping, ping!
Little lights swirled around the Beast.
He floated in the air.
And the Beast turned back into a handsome prince!
Lumière, Mrs Potts, Cogsworth and Chip became people again too.
The castle became bright and beautiful.
And Belle and the prince danced, and lived happily ever after.
With lots and lots of books, of course.
